analyticalQuestion: How can matched Fourier support and coefficient moduli coexist with a growing phase-sensitive heat-flow separation?
supportedClaim: The explicit Dirichlet and Rudin-Shapiro tensor fields have identical Fourier support and coefficient moduli, while their analytic heat-flow scaling guides differ by m^(2/3); after a common amplitude scaling, the Rudin-Shapiro guide tends to zero and the Dirichlet guide stays order one.
